question: Does a bounded Native qsearch run on a complete-history Shogi continuous-check fixture diverge from Core?
scope: One existing standard-Shogi checking cycle, finite depth and qsearch limits, zero test evaluator. The selected PV does not force the perpetual-check line; this is result parity on the full-history root, not proof of a particular q-node trace or strength.

source_review.qsearch_terminal_authority: gc_semantic_quiescence checks gc_semantic_terminal_status_known at node entry; non-deferred child transitions use full checked history.
source_review.history_deferral_guard: The fixture has repetition_limit 4 and history multiplicity 3; gc_semantic_q_history_deferrable refuses the transient quiet-history path when any recorded identity reaches repetition_limit - 1.
source_review.conclusion: No observed Core/Native result divergence. The line's exact terminal transition is independently certified, but the returned best PV avoids it; do not claim a forced terminal q-child trace. No production change is justified by this bounded check.
